name: Microsoft 365
problem: People lose time switching tools, finding documents, and coordinating everyday work.
solution: Bring email, meetings, documents, and collaboration into a managed workplace. Align Microsoft 365 apps, content ownership, and adoption with the way teams actually work.

name: Viva
problem: Employees struggle to find company resources, connect with colleagues, and access relevant learning.
solution: Use Connections for employee resources, Engage for communities, Learning for development, and Insights for appropriately governed workplace analysis. Set content ownership and privacy requirements before rollout.

name: Teams
problem: Conversations, meetings, and project decisions are scattered across disconnected channels.
solution: Organize chat, meetings, calling, and shared workspaces around teams and business processes. Establish workspace ownership and clear collaboration practices.

name: SharePoint
problem: Shared documents and company knowledge are difficult to organize, maintain, and find.
solution: Create managed sites, document libraries, and intranet experiences with appropriate permissions, ownership, and information structure.

name: OneDrive
problem: Individual work files are trapped on devices or shared through uncontrolled copies.
solution: Provide managed file storage, synchronization, and sharing for individual work, with collaboration and recovery capabilities that depend on configuration.

name: Exchange
problem: Email, calendars, and mailbox administration need consistent ownership and reliable operation.
solution: Manage organizational messaging and scheduling, including mailbox access, mail flow, and supported retention and protection settings.

name: Windows 365
problem: Employees need a consistent Windows workspace without depending entirely on a particular physical device.
solution: Provide cloud-hosted personal computers, called Cloud PCs, that users can access from supported devices. Select the right edition and plan identity, provisioning, networking, and support.

name: Intune
problem: Unmanaged devices and inconsistent application settings create support and security gaps.
solution: Manage supported devices and applications, apply configuration and compliance policies, and coordinate access requirements with identity and security teams.

name: Windows Autopilot
problem: Preparing new or reassigned Windows devices requires too much manual setup.
solution: Streamline supported device provisioning and enrollment into organizational management. Plan prerequisites, deployment profiles, and exception handling.

name: Entra
problem: Organizations need to control who can access applications and information without granting unnecessary network access.
solution: Entra combines identity and access capabilities. Plan identity lifecycle, sign-in risk, application access, and secure connectivity together rather than treating them as separate permission systems. Apply Zero Trust principles: verify explicitly, use least-privilege access, and assume breach when designing controls.
details: Entra ID manages identities, authentication, and application access; ID means identity in these product names.
Entra ID Governance supports access reviews and lifecycle processes. Entra ID Protection identifies identity risk. Conditional Access applies access decisions using configured signals and policies.
Entra Private Access provides Zero Trust Network Access for supported private applications. Entra Internet Access provides a secure web gateway for internet and cloud-service traffic.

Entra Suite brings capabilities together under a licensing offer. Validate prerequisites and replace eligible virtual private network access in stages, not as an assumption that every network connection can be removed.

name: Purview
problem: Sensitive information is difficult to discover, classify, protect, and govern across its lifecycle.
solution: Connect data classification, information protection, data loss prevention, and supported compliance capabilities to business handling requirements. Licensing and workload support determine the available controls.
details: Discovery and governance: identify data owners, locate sensitive information, and use catalog and lineage context to guide decisions about trust, access, and reuse across supported sources.

Information protection: define classifications and sensitivity labels, then apply data loss prevention controls to supported collaboration and data movement. Test policies against real work before broader enforcement.

Compliance and investigations: plan retention, audit, eDiscovery, and insider risk capabilities with legal and privacy owners. Product configuration supports those processes; it does not establish compliance by itself.

AI readiness: review oversharing and how assistants use protected information. Agree evidence, exceptions, and ownership, then prioritize improvements rather than assuming every connected application enforces identical controls.

name: Defender
problem: Threat signals across devices, email, identities, and cloud workloads are fragmented.
solution: Use the relevant Defender products to prevent, detect, investigate, and respond to threats across supported workloads.
details: Extended detection and response (XDR) connects related signals and investigations through Defender XDR.
Defender for Endpoint protects supported endpoints. Defender for Office 365 addresses threats in email and collaboration.
Defender for Cloud addresses cloud security posture and workload protection. Coverage depends on enabled plans and connected workloads.

Security for AI connects threat detection with Entra identity controls, Purview data protection, and AI Governance. Define coverage and response ownership across these layers rather than relying on a single product.

name: Sentinel
problem: Security teams need a coordinated view of threats across multiple systems and data sources.
solution: Bring security information and event management together with investigation and response workflows. Prioritize relevant telemetry, tune detections, and govern automated actions.
details: Connect relevant logs from cloud services, identities, applications, and existing security tools, with deliberate retention and ingestion-cost planning.
Engineer detections, investigate correlated incidents, and hunt for threats using contextual evidence rather than treating every alert as an isolated event.
Coordinate supported automation and response playbooks. Require approval for disruptive actions, and define escalation paths, response owners, and measures of investigation quality.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
problem: People spend too much time gathering work context, drafting content, and making sense of information.
solution: Use an artificial intelligence assistant integrated with work applications and permission-aware organizational context. Copilot is a product experience, not a single model; useful results still depend on data quality, appropriate access, and review.
details: Architecture and permissions: models use grounding and Graph to work with organizational context within the signed-in user's permissions. Review oversharing before rollout; existing access is not automatically appropriate access.
Copilot Chat and Microsoft 365 Copilot offer different experiences. Work-data grounding and supported model choices depend on licensing, application context, availability, and administrator settings.

Readiness and adoption: confirm prerequisites, licensing, security configuration, and content ownership. Pilot representative tasks, train users to review results, and define support and success measures before expanding.

name: Copilot Studio
problem: Teams need assistants tailored to their own knowledge and business processes.
solution: Build and manage agents with configured knowledge, tools, workflows, and supported model choices. Define permissions, approvals, evaluation, and support before allowing consequential actions.
details: Model selection: compare supported models and external providers against task quality, regional availability, prerelease limitations, and administrator controls. Model choices are product-specific, not unrestricted interchangeability.

name: Agent 365
problem: A growing agent estate makes ownership, visibility, and oversight difficult to maintain.
solution: Support agent inventory, lifecycle management, governance, and security oversight across supported integrations. Align licensing and configuration with the organization's control requirements.
details: Adoption needs more than an inventory: agree implementation stages, accountable owners, user training, support, and measures of quality and business value. Use pilot evidence to decide when agents are ready for wider use.

name: Agent Framework
problem: Custom agent workflows need clear coordination between models, tools, and software steps.
solution: Use a development framework to organize agents and workflows, including handoffs and tool integration. The application design must still enforce access, approvals, failure handling, and operational ownership.
details: Model Context Protocol connects applications to tools and information exposed by servers. For supported integrations, validate server trust, permissions, and tool inputs; the protocol does not replace authorization or approval controls.

name: Dynamics 365
problem: Business records and processes are fragmented across sales, service, finance, and operations.
solution: Connect business applications to the relevant process and data model. Choose the applications that fit the scope rather than assuming every Dynamics 365 capability is included in one deployment.

name: Power Platform
problem: Teams need practical ways to build applications, automate work, and analyze information without starting every solution from scratch.
solution: Combine supported low-code capabilities with approved data connections and governance. Define environment ownership, application lifecycle, and security boundaries.

name: Power Apps
problem: Important processes rely on spreadsheets, email, or forms that do not fit the task.
solution: Build low-code business applications around approved data and workflows, with appropriate access, testing, and operational support.

name: Power Automate
problem: Repeated manual steps and handoffs slow work and create avoidable errors.
solution: Automate supported workflows and approvals across connected services. Design for permissions, exceptions, duplicate actions, and human review where required.

name: Azure
problem: Applications need infrastructure and managed services that can be deployed and operated consistently.
solution: Build cloud foundations for compute, networking, storage, data, and application services. Align architecture with security, recovery, cost, and operational responsibilities.
details: Landing zones: establish platform responsibilities, identity, connectivity, governance, security, and workload environments before scaling deployments.
Well-Architected Framework: assess reliability, security, cost optimization, operational excellence, and performance efficiency together. Make tradeoffs explicit and revisit them as workloads change.

name: Azure Policy
problem: Cloud resources drift away from agreed configuration and governance requirements.
solution: Define and assess resource policies, enforce supported requirements, and manage exceptions. A policy assignment still needs ownership and remediation processes.

name: Azure Migrate
problem: Migration decisions lack a reliable view of workloads, dependencies, and readiness.
solution: Discover and assess supported workloads, inform migration planning, and coordinate a staged move. Validate cutover, recovery, and application requirements separately.

name: Azure SQL
problem: Applications need relational databases with a suitable balance of compatibility and managed operations.
solution: Choose from Azure's SQL database offerings for the workload. Structured Query Language (SQL) is the language used to query and manage relational data; migration compatibility and service capabilities vary by offering.

name: Fabric
problem: Data ingestion, engineering, analytics, and reporting are disconnected.
solution: Bring supported data workloads together in an integrated analytics environment. Establish shared definitions, quality, ownership, and access rather than simply moving data into a new platform.

name: OneLake
problem: Separate analytics projects create unnecessary data copies and inconsistent access practices.
solution: Use Fabric's shared logical data lake to organize analytics data. Plan data ownership, access, and supported sharing patterns across workloads.

name: Power BI
problem: Decision-makers spend too much time reconciling reports and interpreting inconsistent metrics.
solution: Build shared data models, reports, and dashboards. Business intelligence (BI) turns data into information for decisions; trusted definitions and appropriate access remain essential.

name: Foundry
problem: Promising artificial intelligence prototypes lack the tooling needed for evaluation and operation.
solution: Develop applications and agents with supported models, tools, evaluation, and monitoring. Select hosting and model options according to workload, security, and operational requirements.

name: GitHub
problem: Software delivery needs traceable changes, collaboration, and repeatable release processes.
solution: Manage source code, reviews, and supported automation for development teams. Configure repository access, release controls, and deployment responsibilities.

name: Azure Monitor
problem: Teams cannot reliably explain application performance or identify operational issues early.
solution: Collect and analyze supported metrics, logs, and traces, then connect alerts to actionable support procedures. Monitoring needs relevant signals and accountable owners.

name: Azure Cost Management
problem: Cloud spending lacks clear allocation, visibility, and ownership.
solution: Analyze supported usage and costs, set budgets, and identify optimization opportunities. Combine cost data with business context rather than treating lower spend as the only goal.

name: Azure Backup
problem: Important workloads need recoverable copies with defined protection and retention requirements.
solution: Protect supported workloads through managed backup capabilities. Agree recovery objectives, secure backup access, and test restoration rather than assuming a successful backup proves recovery.

name: Azure Logic Apps
problem: Systems need integration workflows with clear operational and authorization boundaries.
solution: Coordinate supported service connections and workflow steps, including security automation. Control credentials, error handling, approvals, and changes to connected systems.
